out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: PIC Duties, No Unnecessary Persons
violations.observation: PIC’s sister who does not work at facility was seen in food prep areas and behind the cash register.
violations.corrective_action: Persons unnecessary to the food establishment operation are not allowed in the food preparation, food storage, or ware washing areas of the commercial establishment. Only approved tours or brief visits may be authorized by the Person in Charge or certified food manager if steps are taken to ensure that exposed food, clean equipment/utensils, clean linens, and single service items are protected from contamination. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT NO UNNECESSARY PERSONS ARE ALLOWED IN THE BACK OF FACILITY. PIC ASKED SISTER TO LEAVE THE FOOD PREP AREAS AND FROM BEHIND THE CASH REGISTER AND STAY IN LOBBY ONLY.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Signage
violations.observation: Observed that sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided or is not clearly visible at all handwashing sinks used by food employees.
violations.corrective_action: Provide a visible sign or poster at all handwashing sinks used by food employees that reminds food employees to wash their hands. PLEASE PROVIDE HAND WASHING SIGNAGE BY TIME OF NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours. Cooked chickpeas in the 2DR UPR in supply room was temping at 60F, 12-24 hours after the cooling process had begun.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT DUE TO THE CHICKPEAS NOT PROPERLY COOLING TO 41F IN THE 6 HOUR TIME FRAME, THE FOOD COULD NOW MAKE A CUSTOMER SICK. PIC THREW CHICKPEAS AWAY.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Cooling in Equipment
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: a large batch of cooked chickpeas were in a metal hotel pan that was filled to the top in the 2DR UPR in supply room and did not allow for proper cooling.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC WAYS TO FACILITATE PROPER COOLING. PIC THREW AWAY CHICKPEAS THAT HAD NOT COOLED PROPERLY.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: Single-service items were observed being reused for the storage of multiple food items throughout the facility.
violations.corrective_action: Single-service items may not be reused. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC WHAT CONTAINERS MAY BE REUSED AND WHAT MAY NOT. PIC WILL REPLACE ALL NON-REUSABLE CONTAINERS BY TIME OF NEXT INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use

violations.title: Eating, Drinking, or Using Tobacco
violations.observation: A food employee was observed eating, smoking, or drinking in areas where they may contaminate food, clean equipment, utensils or other items needing protection. OBSERVED EMPLOYEE EATING IN THE KITCHEN AREA AT THE PREP TABLE.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees may only eat, drink, or use tobacco in a designated area like a dining room or office area. Employees shall not eat or drink in the kitchen areas, warewashing areas, or storage areas where items may become contaminated. EHS STOPPED EMPLOYEE & DISCUSSED THAT EATING IS ONLY TO OCCUR IN THE DINING AND/OR EMPLOYEE AREAS

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: various spices in numerous shake containers that were not labeled.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. DISCUSSED WITH CFM THAT ONCE ITEMS ARE REMOVED FROM THE COMMERCIALLY LABELED CONTAINERS THAT THEY MUST BE LABELED IN THE WORKING CONTAINERS.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. OBSERVED TWO LARGE BOWLS OF SOAKING RICE SITTING DIRECTLY ON TOP OF THE FLOOR UNDER A PREP TABLE.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. RECOMMENDED TO CFM THAT THE RICE BE MOVED TO THE PREP TABLE IN THE BACK STORAGE AREA AND NOT DIRECTLY ON THE FLOOR
